framework: US OMB Memorandum M-26-04 (11 December 2025) - Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles
clause_or_page: Agency Actions (a)-(c), p.3; Appendix A s.1 and s.1(A) Minimum Threshold for LLM Transparency, Appendix pp.1-2 of 4
requirement_paraphrase: When procuring an LLM, agencies must obtain enough vendor information to judge compliance with the Unbiased AI Principles; solicitations must at minimum request the acceptable use policy, model/system/data cards (which often include identified risks, mitigations and benchmark evaluation scores), end-user resources and a feedback mechanism. New LLM solicitations must carry contractual compliance requirements, and agency procurement policies had to be updated by 11 March 2026.
what_is_tested: Vendor documentation of LLM risks, mitigations and evaluation results before procurement
who_tests: Procuring agency reviews vendor-supplied documentation; vendor/developer supplies evaluation results
interpretation_note: Binding on executive agencies (not national security systems; open-source-licensed LLMs not required but due diligence advised). A document-request duty, not an agency testing duty. Memo sunsets two years after issuance unless OMB provides otherwise. Complements M-25-22 and builds on M-25-21.

framework: US OMB Memorandum M-26-04 (11 December 2025) - Increasing Public Trust in AI Through Unbiased AI Principles
clause_or_page: Appendix A s.1(B) Threshold for Enhanced LLM Transparency, items (i)(D), (ii)(A)-(B), (iii)(B), Appendix pp.2-3 of 4
requirement_paraphrase: Depending on planned use, an agency may request more information, such as use of red teaming to continuously assess the model for bias, results and methodology of vendor bias evaluations (e.g. prompt pairs on politically oriented topics), benchmark scores on bias, helpfulness, honesty or accuracy (multi-language where needed), and model evaluation tools for comparing outputs or models.
what_is_tested: Vendor bias evaluations, red-teaming and benchmark results for the LLM
who_tests: LLM vendor/developer conducts evaluations; agency reviews disclosed results
interpretation_note: Discretionary ('may decide') within a binding memo, so coded guidance. For agency-developed LLMs, Appendix A s.2(A) expects documentation of how the model was evaluated and whether recurring evaluations are performed.
